title: Hosted API margin thresholds and lifecycle sheet (scratch)
content:
PURPOSE
Quick scratch workbook to anchor margin thresholds and lifecycle triggers for Hosted API SKUs by region/model family. This is intentionally rough: mixes table-style rows with short notes and explicit formulas so eng/product can iterate.

ASSUMPTIONS (global)
- Currency = USD.
- Token convention: 1 token ≈ 4 chars (approx).
- Price inputs are per-1k-tokens (customer billed unit).
- Cost components included: GPU amortization, power, network egress, storage (KV cache), orchestration (pods + control plane), and infra overhead (SRE/tooling).
- Utilization baseline: 68% average for hosted pools unless noted.
- Discounting: regional GCP/AZ prices aggregated into a single regional factor.
- Target gross margin bands: red <25%, yellow 25–40%, green >=40%.

KEY FORMULAS (spreadsheet-ready)
- cost_per_1k = (gpu_hourly_amort / tokens_per_hour) + infra_per_token + average_power_per_token + network_per_token + cache_amort_per_token
- margin_pct = (price_per_1k - cost_per_1k) / price_per_1k
- break_even_price = cost_per_1k / (1 - target_margin)

SAMPLE ROWS (model x region slices)
Columns: Region | Model | GPU | SeqLen P90 | Throughput (tok/s) | tokens_per_hour | gpu_hourly_amort | infra_per_1k | power_per_1k | network_per_1k | cost_per_1k | price_per_1k | margin_pct | margin_band | notes
us-west | redwood-13b-q4f | A10G | 512 | 350 | 1,260,000 | 18.50 | 0.05 | 0.03 | 0.02 | 0.64 | 2.50 | 0.744 | green | baseline slow seq profile
us-west | open-70b-int8 | H100 | 1024 | 420 | 1,512,000 | 42.00 | 0.08 | 0.06 | 0.03 | 1.98 | 3.50 | 0.434 | yellow | high-capacity, high-amort
eu-west | redwood-13b-q4f | A10G | 512 | 330 | 1,188,000 | 20.10 | 0.06 | 0.035 | 0.025 | 0.76 | 2.80 | 0.729 | green | slightly higher cogs
ap-southeast | rw-30b-qat | A100S | 512 | 300 | 1,080,000 | 36.00 | 0.07 | 0.05 | 0.03 | 1.16 | 2.75 | 0.578 | green | regional premium infra

EXPLANATION OF SAMPLE ROWS
- tokens_per_hour approximated as throughput (tok/s) * 3600 * utilization (0.68). For sheet quick-calc we already baked utilization into the tokens_per_hour column.
- gpu_hourly_amort estimated by amortizing instance cost + reserved/spot mix divided by effective GPU hours. Example: h100 amort is higher vs a10g.
- infra_per_1k collapses control-plane + orchestration + storage amortization per 1k tokens.

SENSITIVITY CHECKS (quick scenarios)
1) Price compression: if price_per_1k reduces 20% from current -> recompute margin_pct and flag where margin_band becomes red.
2) Utilization drop: -10pp utilization increases gpu_amort per token by ~15–20% depending on instance.
3) Model swap: moving redwood-13b-q4f -> rw-30b-qat for latency-sensitive traffic: check cost delta and regression risk.

QUICK CALCS (cheat cells)
- If price_per_1k = 2.50 and cost_per_1k = 0.64, margin = (2.5 - 0.64)/2.5 = 0.744 -> 74.4%
- Break-even price for target 40% on cost 1.16 = 1.16 / (1 - 0.4) = 1.933 -> roundup to $1.95 recommended

RECOMMENDATIONS & LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS (product + ops)
1) Margin Floors by SKU: set soft floor alerts when margin < 35% for >72h. Hard floor at 25% -> auto-fallback to cheaper model variant or reduce token cap for new customers.
2) Quantization trigger: if margin_landscape shows >10% margin improvement by deploying q6/q4 variants with <3% quality degradation on core eval set -> schedule canary rollout.
3) Regional routing: for models with margin_band red in APAC, route non-SLA traffic to dedicated cheaper variants or to burst capacity for latency-tolerant loads.
4) Price anchoring: for enterprise committed customers, price_per_1k should include minimum 20% reserved discount but maintain >30% margin post-discount via capacity pledge or commit-based pricing.

OPEN QUESTIONS (for next working session)
- How to best attribute KV-cache hits vs cold inference cost in per-1k token math? (need tracing hook to separate cached token counts)
- Should we include data transfer costs for embeddings-heavy customers differently?
- What is a conservative amortization window for new GPU types (12 vs 36 months)?

ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS
- Marcus: add per-model sequence-length distribution columns to sheet (due 2026-03-05).
- Emily: instrument a tracing sample to split cached vs compute tokens (POC by 2026-03-12).
- Diego: produce regional price factors for APAC, EU, US (include committed discounts) and update infra_per_1k (due 2026-03-08).
- Aisha (owner): consolidate scenario deck with 3 price bands and routing recommendations for biz review (2026-03-15).

NOTES TO SELF / SCRATCH
- Keep table wide but maintain canonical 1k-token normalization column; downstream dashboards expect that unit.
- Add an additional sheet with a Monte Carlo sim later (sample variance on seq len, utilization, instance spot mix).
- This doc is a working artifact: expect churn, keep an "archived" snapshot before any major policy change.

END OF SHEET (scratch)
